text.en: Seats on a Ferris wheel lie on a circle. Joining some seats gives chords and quadrilaterals whose angles obey neat rules.

The distance from the centre to any point on the circle is the radius; a chord joins two points on the circle; the longest chord is the diameter.
The perpendicular from the centre to a chord bisects the chord.
Equal chords are equally distant from the centre, and chords equidistant from the centre are equal.
The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference on the same arc.
Angles in the same segment are equal, and the angle in a semicircle is a right angle.
A cyclic quadrilateral has all four vertices on a circle, and its opposite angles add up to 180 degrees.
The converse holds: if the opposite angles of a quadrilateral add to 180 degrees, it is cyclic.

problem.en: In a cyclic quadrilateral ABCD angle A = 80 degrees and angle B = 100 degrees. Find angles C and D.

text.en: Opposite angles add to 180: angle C = 180 - 80 = 100 degrees.

prompt.en: State the key angle properties of a circle.

requiredIdeas.en: Perpendicular from centre bisects a chord
Angle at centre is twice angle at circumference
Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add to 180

points.en: Perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord.
Angle at the centre = 2 x angle at the circumference.
Cyclic quadrilateral: opposite angles add to 180 degrees.
